name: Soul Asylum
label: Twin/Tone
lede: A Minneapolis punk band that cut three releases in 1986 for Twin/Tone, then went to No. 5 and won a Grammy with a song written on a napkin.

eras.title: Three friends, one drum kit
eras.text: A drummer who sings, a bassist who had to learn bass, and a guitarist playing since he was 13. They call themselves Loud Fast Rules, put two songs on a cassette compilation, and change the name before anyone signs them.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Loud Fast Rules: [[Dave Pirner|8849e71c-181b-444b-8cfb-09445e6231d4]] on drums, [[Dan Murphy|06806bee-5233-4c4e-b644-2243620278db]] on guitar
years.p: [[Karl Mueller|dde72be5-d90f-4390-b441-bb8288ec0404]] plays bass in a band whose name is the entire plan. Pirner insists on drumming, and singing, for the first year.
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever he first saw Pirner's band at Zoogy's around 1981, and that the trio came together within four weeks. Mueller had come back from England in 1978 a punk convert and, per the same interview, did not yet play an instrument. Murphy says he eventually talked Pirner into moving off the drum stool to focus on singing and songwriting.

Wikipedia lists Pat Morley as an original drummer in this line-up, which does not sit easily with Murphy's account of Pirner drumming that first year.

years.src: Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Two songs on a cassette called Barefoot and Pregnant
years.p: Loud Fast Rules make their recorded debut on a Reflex Records cassette compilation, then appear on a second one, Kitten, billed as Proud Crass Fools.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Kitten was recorded live at Goofy's Upper Deck, and the band's name on the sleeve is Proud Crass Fools. Both tapes were local Reflex Records releases.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography
years.h: Loud Fast Rules becomes Soul Asylum
years.p: Pirner moves to rhythm guitar, Pat Morley takes the drums, and the title of one of Pirner's songs becomes the band's name.
years.xp: Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever the name came from a Pirner song and that the label suggested the change. Wikipedia dates the rename to 1983; the band's own site says the same.

eras.title: Twin/Tone, and Bob Mould's schedule
eras.text: The label that already has the Replacements signs a band with no album. Hüsker Dü's Bob Mould produces two of their records on budgets of a few thousand dollars, and the drummer chair changes hands.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Twin/Tone Records
years.h: [[Peter Jesperson|00cefb4a-65c2-4faa-812a-8f182b5bc8e9]] signs them to Twin/Tone
years.p: The Minneapolis label, co-founded by Jesperson in 1977 and home to [[The Replacements|dc0d05ce-2f47-4962-b4fa-8631a0a51987]], takes on Soul Asylum before they have released an album.
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever that landing the deal was "bigger than getting signed at Columbia or Big Six" for the band. He also says that despite making records on minimal budgets, he never received a royalty check from the label.

Twin/Tone Records was founded in 1977 by Jesperson, Charley Hallman and Paul Stark, and by 1984 had put out 41 records with three paid staff, according to Wikipedia.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Say What You Will · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum · Twin/Tone Digital: Soul Asylum
years.h: Say What You Will: Karl sells the truck
years.p: The title is a receipt: bassist Karl Mueller sold the band's Chevrolet pickup to buy a bigger Dodge van for the 1984 tours. [[Bob Mould|d7f5305a-15fc-4af4-a61b-f6f45510cc8f]] produced.
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever the first two records ran on budgets of about $4,000, and that Mould "didn't even show up" for the first day of the debut. Wikipedia credits Mould as producer with Blake Gumprecht as co-producer and Steve Fjelstad as engineer.

According to Wikipedia, the original pressing moved 6,738 vinyl copies and 2,639 cassettes. A 1988 CD reissue added five unreleased tracks and became Say What You Will, Clarence...Karl Sold the Truck. Trouser Press hears it as the end of the band's "hardcore slop phase".

years.h: Grant Young replaces Pat Morley on drums
years.p: Morley quits after the first record. Young, who will stay until 1995, takes over.

eras.title: Three releases and 112 shows
eras.text: A record released in January, a cassette in June, another album in November, and a van in between. Opening for Hüsker Dü and headlining a First Avenue circuit turns Soul Asylum into a working band with nothing left in the tank.

years.src: Wikipedia: Made to Be Broken · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Made to Be Broken: Mould again, with Young's drums
years.p: Recorded in 1985, it is the first record with Grant Young and the first of three Soul Asylum releases in 1986.
years.xp: Trouser Press calls it "an essential Soul Asylum LP" and points to "raging dual vocals and interwoven guitar work" between Pirner and Murphy, with "Tied to the Tracks" and "Ship of Fools" as highlights. The Spin Alternative Record Guide credits Young's "off-kilter, rhythmic swerve".

years.cap: Soul Asylum playing on an outdoor stage at the Mayo Civic Center in... · Wikimedia
years.src: EnterTheSoulAsylum: 1986 shows · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Opening for Hüsker Dü on the Flip Your Wig tour
years.p: La Crosse, Madison, Milwaukee and Chicago in January, then Boston, New York, Philadelphia and Athens, Georgia, in front of the band whose singer had produced their records.
years.xp: The fan-run EnterTheSoulAsylum show archive lists the Hüsker Dü dates across January and February 1986. Mould had produced both of Soul Asylum's Twin/Tone albums up to that point.

years.src: Wikipedia: Time's Incinerator · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Time's Incinerator: a cassette-only grab bag
years.p: Twin/Tone puts outtakes, B-sides and Loud Fast Rules-era demos on cassette only, including a James Brown cover by Mueller.
years.xp: The last track on side two is an improvised live set by Madison hardcore band Mecht Mensch, recorded when a shared bill hit technical trouble. Trouser Press describes the tape as outtakes, covers and live material from 1980 to 1986. The Spin Alternative Record Guide gave it 5/10.

years.src: EnterTheSoulAsylum: 1986 shows
years.h: TSOL cancels, so Soul Asylum play before Bad Brains
years.p: At First Avenue, the fan-run show archive says the night ends with the drummer alone on stage.
years.xp: The same archive counts 112 Soul Asylum shows in 1986, coast to coast. On May 20 the band won best Garage Band at the Minnesota Music Awards alongside Hüsker Dü, and the archive's diary entry calls Pirner's acceptance speech "crazy".

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: While You Were Out · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: While You Were Out: two months, between tours
years.p: Chris Osgood produces the year's third release. Robert Christgau gives it a B+; Trouser Press hears "thin, messy production".
years.xp:
Murphy told Perfect Sound Forever the record was rushed in two months while the band was touring, and that the result disappointed them. The New York Times, quoted on Wikipedia, called the sound "explosive speed-rock in jubilant major keys".

The Wildhearts covered "The Judge" in 1992, and Automatic 7 later recorded "Closer to the Stars".

eras.title: The A&M detour
eras.text: A major label signs the band, then loses interest in the person who signed them. Twin/Tone still gets one more record out, with its own logo on a Herb Alpert parody.

years.src: Perfect Sound Forever · Wikipedia: Hang Time · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Hang Time: A&M's champion leaves before it ships
years.p: [[Ed Stasium|23336099-24e0-40e7-af6d-a224bcdb4e41]] and [[Lenny Kaye|47455aa4-c71e-4662-a775-33b81fcf0a37]] produce the major-label debut. Murphy says A&M's support faded when A&R man Steve Ralbovsky left four weeks before release.
years.xp:
Murphy's own "Cartoon" is one of three singles alongside "Marionette" and "Little Too Clean". Trouser Press credits the record with "unprecedented sonic excellence"; Robert Christgau gave it a B-.

Murphy also says Columbia's Donnie Ienner later signed the band after hearing a demo that included "Runaway Train".

years.src: Wikipedia: Clam Dip & Other Delights · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Clam Dip & Other Delights: Mueller in whipped cream and seafood
years.p: The cover parodies Herb Alpert's Whipped Cream & Other Delights as a nod to the band's new label, A&M, with Twin/Tone's logo where A&M's would go.
years.xp:
Mueller replaced the original cover's model and, per Wikipedia, spent hours in a mixture of sour cream, paint, whipped cream and seafood. Recorded 1987-88 with Tom Herbers, the EP includes "P-9", written for the striking Hormel workers in Austin, Minnesota.

The UK edition added covers of Foreigner and Janis Joplin; the US edition kept only "Chains".

years.src: Wikipedia: And the Horse They Rode In On · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: And the Horse They Rode In On: live on an A&M soundstage
years.p: Steve Jordan, drummer with Keith Richards' X-pensive Winos, produces; most of it is cut live in Los Angeles and finished in Cannon Falls, Minnesota.
years.xp: The band mounted a North American tour behind it. The Windsor Star called Murphy's "Gullible's Travels" "one of the best half-dozen rock tracks of the year", and Trouser Press names "Easy Street" "an instant SA anthem".
play: And the Horse They Rode In On

eras.title: Runaway Train
eras.text: A new label, a new producer and a drummer who plays only some of his own record. A ballad Pirner wrote alone on an acoustic guitar goes to No. 5 and wins a Grammy, and the band spends the next decade being asked about it.

years.src: SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · Request Magazine, July 1995 · Wikipedia: Grant Young · Wikipedia: Grave Dancers Union
years.h: Five songs in, a session drummer takes over from Grant Young
years.p: Producer Michael Beinhorn finds Young's takes lackluster and brings in Sterling Campbell; they split the drumming, but Campbell is credited only as "percussionist".
years.xp:
Murphy said in SPIN's oral history: "We were all Minneapolis boys...we resisted it." Young says he played on five or six songs. Booker T. Jones cut keyboards in Los Angeles a week after the 1992 riots; Beinhorn says he played on seven songs in five hours.

In Request in July 1995 Pirner said of Young: "Grant, who was my best friend, my drummer for 10 years - I love the guy still." He added: "We didn't have the faith in him that we should've had." Young later ran a Boundary Waters resort near Ely, Minnesota, with his wife Catherine, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: Grave Dancers Union · Request Magazine, July 1995
years.h: Grave Dancers Union reaches No. 11 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Recorded in three studios with Beinhorn, it also tops the Heatseekers chart; the cover is a 1970 photograph by Jan Saudek.
years.xp: Murphy told Request: "I don't think up until [Grave Dancers Union] we even made a good record." Entertainment Weekly gave it an A and Rolling Stone 3.5 stars, per Wikipedia, and it went double platinum in the US.

years.h: "Somebody to Shove" hits No. 1 on Modern Rock
years.p: The first single from Grave Dancers Union spends a week on top of Billboard's chart, in a video directed by Zack Snyder.

years.src: SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
yt: Somebody to Shove, live at the MTV Inaugural Ball
years.h: Playing Bill Clinton's inauguration
years.p: Soul Asylum perform at Clinton's first inauguration, a few months after "Somebody to Shove" topped the Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: Murphy told SPIN the band also played the White House lawn, and that Clinton was "very funny, charming, and nice" during a 25-minute visit.

years.h: MTV Unplugged puts "Black Gold" on acoustic guitars
years.p: The 1993 set includes the Grave Dancers Union track "Black Gold", which Zack Snyder also directed a video for.

q: It overshadowed everything else we did.
years.src: Guitar Player: Dave Pirner Reveals · Wikipedia: Runaway Train · SPIN: Wrong Way on a One-Way Track · All That's Interesting: Runaway Train
years.h: "Runaway Train" goes to No. 5 with missing kids on screen
years.p: Director Tony Kaye runs photographs of missing children, and MTV cuts the on-screen plea for tips over fears it will read as a public service announcement.
years.xp:
Pirner has said he wrote the song around what he now calls undiagnosed depression, on a napkin, after a breakdown over fears of losing his hearing. Guitar Player reports he recorded the acoustic parts on a rented Gibson J-200. The demo, with producer Brian Paulson, was two acoustic guitars and harmony vocals, and the final arrangement barely changed.

All That's Interesting reports Kaye made three versions with 36 children each, using photographs from the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Kaye has said 21 to 26 of them were found, and calls the video "the single most important thing that happened in the history of MTV".

All That's Interesting also notes that several children counted as found had left home on their own, some fleeing abuse, and that not all were glad to see themselves in the video.

years.h: "Runaway Train" wins the 1994 Grammy for Best Rock Song
years.p: The award goes to Pirner as the song's writer, for a band that started out as Loud Fast Rules.

eras.title: The hangover
eras.text: Butch Vig in Madison, a drummer Pirner calls his best friend gone, and a follow-up that goes platinum but not to the places the last one did. Then a benefit prom, and a record that ends the Columbia deal.

years.src: Wikipedia: Let Your Dim Light Shine · Request Magazine, July 1995 · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: Let Your Dim Light Shine: Butch Vig, Madison, No. 6
years.p: Recorded at Smart Studios with Sterling Campbell as the full-time drummer; "Misery" reaches No. 20 on the Hot 100 and tops Modern Rock.
years.xp:
Pirner told Request: "Making this record was just a bitch, quite frankly." He said the band "really took an easy way out" in dropping Grant Young, who had been drumming for the band for ten years. Trouser Press hears Pirner "straining to sound like himself", and reports critics attacked it as a sellout.

The album went platinum in the US.

years.src: Wikipedia: After the Flood · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Trouser Press: Soul Asylum
years.h: A prom in an Air Force hangar, two months after the flood
years.p: Soul Asylum play a joint high school prom at Grand Forks Air Force Base for students whose own prom was cancelled by the Red River flood.
years.xp: The recording came out seven years later as After the Flood: Live from the Grand Forks Prom, June 28, 1997 (Columbia/Legacy, October 5, 2004). It runs 19 tracks, with covers of Smokey Robinson, Marvin Gaye and Alice Cooper, and the back cover shows the burnt-out Security Building, photographed by Eric Hylden for the Grand Forks Herald.

years.src: Wikipedia: Candy from a Stranger · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Candy from a Stranger stalls at No. 121
years.p: Chris Kimsey produces; "I Will Still Be Laughing" plays over the credits of BASEketball and is the band's last single on Billboard's rock charts.
years.xp: Pitchfork gave it 2.5 out of 10 and Robert Christgau called it a "dud", per Wikipedia. Wikipedia reports Columbia dropped the band after it underperformed. Ian Mussington was the drummer from 1998 to 2005.

eras.title: For Karl
eras.text: A benefit, a death, and a record finished around a bass player who was not there. The Replacements' Tommy Stinson and Prince's drummer Michael Bland help carry it.

years.cap: Benefit for Karl Mueller, the Quest, Minneapolis, October 2004
years.src: Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: A benefit puts Bob Mould and Grant Hart on one stage
years.p: Mueller, diagnosed with throat cancer that May, gets a Quest benefit where Mould and [[Grant Hart|571e1aad-0512-45ec-a26d-1d09d786cc53]] play together for the first time in sixteen years.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Gear Daddies and [[Paul Westerberg|d558f844-4db0-4bc3-ba22-49ad2ca2722e]] on the bill and says the night raised more than $50,000. Mould had produced Soul Asylum's first two records.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Soul Asylum's Mueller Dead · AV Club: Interview: Dave Pirner · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: Karl Mueller dies of throat cancer at 41
years.p: The bassist, a founder since Loud Fast Rules, dies at home. Rolling Stone reports a memorial service at Lakewood Cemetery Chapel.
years.xp: In a July 2006 interview Pirner said: "His contribution was always to inspire and to make sure nobody took themselves too seriously." His widow Mary Beth founded the cancer nonprofit Kill Kancer in his memory in 2014, per Wikipedia.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Silver Lining · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum
years.h: The Silver Lining finishes what Mueller started
years.p: Recorded 2004-06 with John Fields and Steve Hodge, it is the first studio album in eight years; Mueller plays on most tracks and Tommy Stinson and Fields fill in the rest.
years.xp:
Murphy says on the band's site: "For me, this record is Karl." ABC and ESPN used "Stand Up and Be Strong" in college football coverage that season, and Prince later covered it on his posthumous 2021 album Welcome 2 America.

Stinson, the Replacements bassist, and Michael Bland, formerly Prince's drummer, joined in late 2005. During Stinson's Guns N' Roses work, George Scot McKelvey and later Pete Donnelly covered bass.

eras.title: Same name, new room
eras.text: The last founding guitarist retires, the bass chair turns over again, and Pirner keeps making records under the name, most recently from Minneapolis after leaving New Orleans.

years.src: Wikipedia: Dan Murphy · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Star Tribune: Soul Asylum reacts · EnterTheSoulAsylum: Biography
years.h: Dan Murphy retires after Delayed Reaction
years.p: The founding guitarist leaves weeks after the album on 429 Records; his cousin Justin Sharbono takes over, and Winston Roye replaces Tommy Stinson on bass.
years.xp:
Murphy's statement said staying in music takes "naivety and swagger. I no longer have either." He donated the Gibson Les Paul he used on every Soul Asylum album to the Minnesota Historical Society and now runs Grapefruit Moon Gallery in Minneapolis. Stinson left over his Guns N' Roses commitments.

Ryan Smith replaced Sharbono in 2016, and Jeremy Tappero has played bass since 2020.

years.src: Wikipedia: Hurry Up and Wait · Wikipedia: Soul Asylum · Please Kill Me: Loud Fast Words
years.h: Hurry Up and Wait lands as COVID shuts the tour down
years.p: The twelfth album, made at Nicollet Studios with John Fields, comes out on Blue Élan after Pirner's divorce and move from New Orleans to Minnesota.
years.xp: AllMusic's Mark Deming credits Pirner with a "more pensive and introspective side". The tour stopped in mid-March 2020, and Pirner and Ryan Smith livestreamed through the shutdown. The band played live again on June 26, 2021, opening for the BoDeans in New Lenox, Illinois; the thirteenth album, Slowly but Shirley, followed in 2024.
